framework: FBISE Assessment Framework (National Curriculum of Pakistan 2022-23)
subject: Mathematics

source.publisher: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
source.licence: Government publication; structure + our own wording only

outcomes.text: Recall function as a rule, with domain, co-domain, range, one-one and onto.
Know linear, quadratic and square root functions.
Define inverse functions and show their domain and range.
Interpret the relation between a one-one function and its inverse on a graph.
Sketch graphs of linear and non-linear functions.
Plot y = x^n for integer and rational n.
Plot quadratic functions of the form ax^2+bx+c.
Draw a graph using factors.
Predict a quadratic function from its graph using the factor form.
Find intersection points graphically of lines, and of a line with a quadratic.
Solve everyday problems graphically.
Draw the graph of the modulus function.
Show graph transformations: horizontal shift, vertical shift and scaling.
Classify functions as algebraic or transcendental.
Describe trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions.
Identify domain and range of basic transcendental functions.
Show understanding of logarithms.
Derive and apply product, quotient and power laws of logarithms.
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions and use them for compound interest.
Solve exponential and logarithmic equations.
Find the limit of a sequence and of a function.
Apply limit theorems for sum, difference, product and quotient to algebraic, exponential and trigonometric functions.
Test continuity and discontinuity of a function at a point and on an interval.
Apply transcendental functions, limits and continuity to real-world problems.
Calculate inflation over time.
Calculate depreciation by straight-line, sum-of-years-digits and production-unit methods.

subtopics.title: Gradient and derivative at a point

outcomes.text: Recognise the tangent to a curve at a point.
Calculate the gradient of a curve at a point.
Identify the derivative as the limit of a difference quotient.
Calculate the derivative of a function at a point.
Estimate the derivative as a rate of change.
Recognise the derivative function.
Find the derivative of a square root function.
Find the derivative of a quadratic function.
State the link between derivatives and continuity.
State, prove and apply the constant, coefficient, power, sum, product and quotient rules.
Extend the power rule to negative exponents.
Combine rules to differentiate polynomial and rational functions.
Apply rates of change to displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Differentiate trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions.
Differentiate exponential functions.
Differentiate logarithmic functions.
Use differentiation to find where functions increase or decrease.
Find equations of tangent and normal to a curve.
Apply differentiation to real-world problems.
Find higher order derivatives of algebraic, implicit, parametric and transcendental functions.
Approximate functions locally by linear functions.
Explain differentials and use them to approximate change.
Calculate relative and percentage error from a differential approximation.
Illustrate global and local extrema.
Find extreme values with the second derivative test.
Explain how to find critical points over a closed interval.
Use critical points to locate absolute extrema.
Apply derivatives to maximum and minimum problems.
Apply higher order derivatives to real-life problems.
Find the general antiderivative of a function.
Recognise terms and notation for antiderivatives.
State the power rule for integrals.
State and apply properties of indefinite integrals.
State the definition of the definite integral.
Explain integrand, limits and variable of integration.
State and apply properties of definite integrals.
Use the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals.
Describe the link between definite integral and net area.
Find area bounded by curves and lines.
Find volume of revolution about an axis.
Use the trapezium rule to estimate a definite integral.
Apply integration to real-world problems.
Distinguish scalar distance and speed from vector displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Sketch and interpret displacement-time and velocity-time graphs.
Use differentiation and integration in time to solve motion problems.
Use formulae for constant acceleration in a straight line.
Apply mechanics to real-life problems.
Use trigonometric relationships to evaluate integrals.
Integrate exponential and logarithmic functions.
Identify when to use integration by parts.
Apply integration by parts to definite integrals.
Solve integrals using trigonometric substitution.
Integrate a rational function by partial fractions.
Apply integration to real-life problems.
Identify and construct first order differential equations from practical situations.
Solve separable and homogeneous first order equations.
Apply first order equations to growth, decay, cooling and circuits.
Search for roots of an equation graphically or by sign change.
Explain basic principles of solving a nonlinear equation in one variable.
Find real roots by bisection, regula falsi and Newton-Raphson methods.
Apply nonlinear equation solving to real-world problems.
Find the condition for three lines to be concurrent.
Find equations of the median, altitude and right bisector of a triangle.
Show that medians, altitudes and right bisectors of a triangle are concurrent.
Find the area of a triangle from its vertices.
Recognise homogeneous linear and quadratic equations in two variables.
Show that a homogeneous second degree equation gives two lines through the origin and find the angle between them.
Apply analytical geometry to real-world problems.
Explain the need for vector valued functions.
Construct a vector valued function.
Identify domain and range of vector valued functions.
Tell scalar valued from vector valued functions.
Explain the derivative of a vector function of one variable.
Use vector differentiation for velocity and acceleration.
Apply vector valued functions to real-world problems.
Find domains and ranges of principal and inverse trigonometric functions.
Draw graphs of the six inverse trigonometric functions.
State, prove and apply addition and subtraction formulae for inverse trig functions.
Solve equations like sin x = k using periodic, even/odd and translation properties.
Solve basic trigonometric equations graphically.
Use periods to find general solutions of trigonometric equations.
Apply inverse trigonometric functions to real-world problems.
Demonstrate conics: circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola.
Derive and apply the standard equation of a circle.
Find the equation of a circle from three points or other given conditions.

subtopics.title: Tangent and normal to a circle

outcomes.text: Find conditions for a line to meet or touch a circle.
Find the tangent in slope form and the normal to a circle.
Find the length of a tangent from an external point.
Derive and apply the standard equation of a parabola.
Sketch parabolas and find their elements.
Find the equation of a parabola from focus, vertex or directrix.

subtopics.title: Tangent and normal to a parabola

outcomes.text: Find the tangency condition for a line and parabola and write the slope-form tangent.
Find the tangent and normal to a parabola at a point.
Derive and apply the standard equation of an ellipse and identify its elements.
Convert to standard ellipse form, find elements and draw the graph.

subtopics.title: Tangent and normal to an ellipse

outcomes.text: Find intersections of an ellipse with a line, including tangency.
Find the tangent to an ellipse in point-slope form.
Find the tangent and normal to an ellipse at a point.
Derive and apply the standard equation of a hyperbola and identify its elements.
Find the equation of a hyperbola from given elements.

subtopics.title: Tangent and normal to a hyperbola

outcomes.text: Find intersections of a hyperbola with a line, including tangency.
Find the tangent to a hyperbola in point-slope form.
Find the tangent and normal to a hyperbola at a point.
Apply conics to real-world problems.
